posts.author: MisterGimmick
posts.body:
Hello hello !
i would like to introduce myself
I'm MisterGimmick, 24 yo, French gator and retrogaming enthusiast !
i'm the kind of guy who tried a ton of things on internet, i have a youtube channel, a twitch channel, i tried animation, drawing, and also making games !
around 1 years ago, RPG Maker XP went free on steam, i decided to use it to make a small Earthbound parody game about my discord server, it started as a post project for the joke
and little by little, I refined the game and it became a parody that was a little better made than a troll game. (you can find
the trailer here
but sorry its only in french X) )
Today I really want to try RPG Maker again, but with a more serious and original project.
Thats why i'm here ! making a parody RPG Maker game was not that easy, so for a bigger project i need to find help !
so i'm happy to join this Forum to meet people who work on RPGs too !

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum!
Out of sheer, morbid curiosity (from an ancient school gamer), what do you consider to be "retro games"? Just curious how far back you go for that retro vibe.
My favorite game series has to be the Wizardry series. The first game (W1) came out in 1981 and the last game (W8) came out in 2001. W8 is definitely my favorite.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
Normally, I would consider retro any game that simulates the design and mechanics of games up to the fifth generation, that is, 64-bit.
However, from my current point of view, the simulated reproduction of any mechanic considered classic can be retro, since it revives a past from someone's youth. What company today would make a linear game, with mechanics that resembles God of War,
GTA: SA
, Guilty Gear on PS2?
Of course, there are titles for current consoles that are inspired by third and fourth generation games developed by the companies themselves for current consoles, remembering that there were 2D games for PS2 and PS3. And in that case, these games could be considered retro.
